findings.title: Optical-overshoot law has zero enforcement; adopted at 0 of 23 Avatar call sites
findings.principle: Any component that renders a circular element sized to sit next to a square element of the same box height must apply the shared optical-overshoot correction (lib/optical.ts CIRCLE_OVERSHOOT, 3%) by default, not behind an opt-in boolean prop. Ship a check (in the geometry checker's asymmetric-pairs class) that flags a circle-square sibling pair rendered at equal box height with no overshoot applied, citing lib/optical.ts by name in the failure message.
findings.why: A written law with zero enforcement decays under task focus: an opt-in prop gets forgotten precisely because remembering it carries no cost signal, and that is what happened here. The system's own research names this 'the largest open visual debt in the whole audit' (research/GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES_2026-07-17.md), yet nine days later the fix mechanism exists in code and is used nowhere.
findings.local_evidence: lib/optical.ts:23-36 defines CIRCLE_OVERSHOOT=0.03 and opticalCircleSize(). Avatar.tsx:58,62,64 gates it behind `opticalOvershoot?: boolean`, defaulting to false. `grep -rn '<Avatar' app --include=*.tsx` returns 23 files; `grep -rn 'opticalOvershoot' app --include=*.tsx` returns only Avatar.tsx's own prop declaration and internal usage line, zero call sites pass it.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn 'opticalOvershoot' app lib -> 2 hits, both inside Avatar.tsx's own definition, none at a call site (checked SalonResultCard.tsx, SalonTeam.tsx, SalonReviews.tsx, ProfileTabs.tsx and 19 others via the <Avatar grep list). No LOCKFILE/SOURCE/RATIONALE row states a trigger condition for when the prop must be passed.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: RATIONALE.md:53 and :144 state the 2-4%/4-8% figures and TASTE_LOG.md:187 records the owner's 2026-07-15 approval ('circles next to squares get a small size overshoot'); lib/optical.ts implements the exact formula correctly. The delta: no rule states WHEN a builder must reach for it, and nothing catches the omission.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md section 7 (new row under the layout invariants) plus scripts/check-geometry.mjs's asymmetric-pairs class (already named as a manual 'class (d)' bucket in _geometry-triage.md).
findings.enforcement: gate: extend check-geometry.mjs to flag a rounded-full/circle element adjacent to a square icon/tile of equal box height with no opticalOvershoot applied; today it is doc-only and the prop defaults the wrong way.

findings.title: The DOM-geometry checker exists and produces real signal, but has no committed path from report-only to a gate
findings.principle: A measured layout checker's own file must state the exact exclusion-rule set that separates real defects from structural false positives, and the numeric signal-to-noise threshold under which it may be cited as evidence. Until scripts/check-geometry.mjs implements the exclusion rules already derived in _geometry-triage.md, no PR, mockup, or design-verifier report may cite a raw check-geometry.mjs run as proof of alignment or grid conformance; only the exclusion-filtered defect list counts.
findings.why: A checker that reports 1233 raw findings at ~1.2% actionable signal trains people to ignore it, which is worse than no checker: the next real regression drowns in noise nobody reads anymore. RATIONALE.md already named alignment measurement 'the single biggest honest gap'; shipping an unfiltered checker technically closes that gap on paper while leaving it open in practice.
findings.local_evidence: _geometry-report.md: 'this script never fails the run... Not a gate yet.' _geometry-triage.md: off-grid raw=1233, actionable-after-filtering=191 (15.5%); broken-axis raw=159, actionable=0-9 ('effectively 0% actionable on this 3-route sample... it may simply never have much to say beyond nested-radius/off-grid'). The triage's own opening note confirms scripts/check-geometry.mjs was read but never edited to apply these findings, so the shipped script still emits the unfiltered numbers.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n 'gate' _design-system/_geometry-report.md _design-system/_geometry-triage.md confirms both files explicitly state 'not a gate yet' / a triage layered on top of unmodified checker output, with no promotion criterion written anywhere in LOCKFILE, SOURCE, or RATIONALE.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: research/GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES_2026-07-17.md section 5 proposed the 5 boolean assertions the checker should run; scripts/check-geometry.mjs was subsequently built implementing 3 of them (off-grid, broken-axis, nested-radius) sometime between 2026-07-17 and 2026-07-25. The delta: no exclusion rules coded into the script, no gate-promotion threshold, no rule barring citation of unfiltered output as evidence.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md section 7 (a 'when a checker becomes a gate' clause) plus scripts/check-geometry.mjs itself.
findings.enforcement: gate: once the 7 exclusion rules are coded into the script, wire a maxFindings=0 threshold on the filtered list into the existing visual CI job (.github/workflows/quality.yml).

findings.title: Sticky-positioning plus overflow containing-block interaction has no written law despite a real prior bug
findings.principle: Before adding any overflow value other than visible (overflow-hidden, overflow-x-clip, overflow-y-auto, overflow-scroll) to a container, grep its subtree for a `sticky` descendant. Setting overflow to anything but visible on an ancestor creates a new containing block that can silently strip a descendant's ability to pin, independent of that descendant's own sticky/top declaration. Re-verify the sticky element still pins after the change; if it stops pinning, the overflow value on the ancestor is the cause, not the sticky rule itself.
findings.why: This is pure CSS mechanics, not taste, which is exactly the kind of rule a reusable law should hold rather than leave to individual memory. It already cost a real fix cycle once (V3-D229), and 55 files in this codebase currently carry a sticky element, meaning the same trap can recur anywhere a future PR adds overflow-hidden to an unrelated section for an unrelated reason.
findings.local_evidence: app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonDetailV3.tsx:194-201, verbatim comment: 'V3-D229 (2026-05-27, sidebar rebuild): DROPPED overflow-hidden. It was breaking position: sticky on the desktop SalonSidebar , sidebar wrapper had sticky top-24 but couldn't pin because an ancestor with overflow-hidden creates a new containing block that scoped sticky to the wrong context. Result: sidebar scrolled away with the page instead of staying pinned, hiding Termin buchen CTA.' `grep -rln sticky app --include=*.tsx` returns 55 files.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn -i 'containing block|overflow-hidden.*sticky|sticky.*overflow-hidden|overflow.*breaks.*sticky' _design-system/*.md _rules/*.md CLAUDE.md -> 0 hits anywhere; the only record of this bug is the inline code comment in one file, not indexed in any reusable-law document.
findings.existing_coverage: none for this mechanic. Sticky Z-ORDER and OFFSET are separately locked (LOCKFILE.md:830-835, RATIONALE.md:546-550) and RATIONALE.md:550 even names an adjacent sacrifice ('a future addition can silently collide if its z-index is not chosen against this exact list'), but that concerns z-index stacking order, a different failure class from the overflow/containing-block trap.
findings.where_it_should_live: _rules/LESSONS_LEARNED.md (the CSS mechanic) plus a one-line pointer in _design-system/LOCKFILE.md's sticky-header-offset subsection.
findings.enforcement: checklist item on any PR touching an overflow-* class today; a static gate would need to trace ancestor/descendant sticky relationships across JSX, out of scope for a quick check.

findings.title: No checkable mirror-diff exists for symmetry claims; asymmetric pairs stay a permanent human-eyeball bucket
findings.principle: A claimed-mirrored pair of elements (a card's left vs right padding, an icon pair flanking a title, twin controls) must pass a reflect-and-diff check: read getComputedStyle on both sides, reflect one about the candidate vertical axis, and assert the resulting padding/margin/position values match within 1px. A failing pair is either a real bug (fix it) or was never meant to be symmetric (name that explicitly in the component's doc so it stops being flagged as broken).
findings.why: Solen's own research already established the perceptual stakes: crude mirror symmetry is judged near pre-attentively (~50ms exposure, Huang/Pashler/Junge 2004, cited at RATIONALE.md:53), so an accidentally-broken mirror reads as a mistake exactly as fast as a designed one reads as intentional. Naming the mechanic in prose is necessary but not sufficient without a way to catch a violation before ship.
findings.local_evidence: The shipped checker's broken-axis check (per _geometry-triage.md's own class table) only compares sibling EDGE positions (top/left alignment), never left-vs-right padding/margin symmetry around a claimed mirror axis; the triage document's exhaustive class breakdown of all 159 broken-axis findings never surfaces a padding-symmetry comparison, confirming the gap exists in the shipped tool, not only in the docs.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn -i 'mirror-diff|mirror diff|reflect.*axis' _design-system/*.md -> 0 hits anywhere, including the checker's own documented behavior in _geometry-triage.md.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: research/GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES_2026-07-17.md ADD item 5 proposed this exact mechanism by name ('Add a mirror-diff step: reflect about the candidate vertical axis, diff bounding boxes, report a pixel offset') and RATIONALE.md:53 now states the perceptual why in full, but neither the taste-diagnosis skill nor scripts/check-geometry.mjs implements the actual diff.
findings.where_it_should_live: scripts/check-geometry.mjs (new assertion class) plus ~/.claude/skills/solen-taste-diagnosis (as a measured-walk step).
findings.enforcement: gate: add to check-geometry.mjs once built; until then a checklist item inside solen-taste-diagnosis's measured walk.

findings.title: No law for how a modular grid degrades when its item count isn't a clean multiple of its column count
findings.principle: A grid classified as LOCKFILE's 'modular' type, fed a dynamic or variable-length collection, must name its own last-row rule at build time: either cap the rendered count to a clean multiple of the column count plus an overflow affordance, or explicitly center/justify a short final row, or fall back to a single-column list below a stated item-count floor. A component may never leave a partial last row to default CSS grid placement (left-aligned with trailing empty cells) without that being a named decision in the component's own doc.
findings.why: The three existing solutions to this in the codebase (SalonHero's photo-count branching between 2-photo and 5-photo layouts, SalonPortfolio's 9-item cap with a '+N' overlay, MobileCategoriesRow's fixed 6-tile reorder-only list) are each hand-solved in isolation with no shared name or rule, so the next grid fed genuinely variable data has no pattern to reach for and will ship the default left-aligned orphan by accident rather than by choice.
findings.local_evidence: app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonPortfolio.tsx:105-112 (UniformGrid): `const visible = urls.slice(0, 9)` caps overflow with a '+N' badge for salons with 9+ photos, but for a salon with 4, 5, 7, or 8 uploaded photos (all plausible pre-launch counts, all under the 9-cap so the overlay never triggers), urls.length % 3 is nonzero, producing a 1-2 tile last row in a grid-cols-3 layout with no stated centering rule; the component's own comment documents only the 9-cap-plus-overlay behavior, not the sub-9 remainder case.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn -i 'orphan|last row|odd number of|grid degrad|single item|widowed' _design-system/*.md CLAUDE.md -> only unrelated 'orphan' hits about orphaned CODE or FILES (LOCKFILE.md:112 the retired s-amber token, REMOVED.md's orphaned pages), zero hits about grid-cell last-row orphaning.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: LOCKFILE.md's Grid TYPE classification (owner-approved 2026-07-16) states WHEN to reach for a modular grid but never what it must do at a non-multiple item count; CLAUDE.md's density-floor law (FLOORS LAW 3) sets a MINIMUM viewport item count but says nothing about the remainder math for whatever count actually renders above that floor.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md, new subsection immediately under the existing 'Grid TYPE classification' block.
findings.enforcement: checklist: name the last-row behavior in the same design note as the grid-TYPE declaration, extending the existing 2026-07-16 owner rule; not mechanically gate-able without knowing the intended vs actual live data count per route.

findings.title: axe-core target-size is not wired into CI despite Solen already running the exact infrastructure it needs
findings.principle: Run @axe-core/playwright's target-size rule (runsOnly: ['target-size']) against the same route list already covered by the visual-regression Playwright job, failing CI on any interactive control under the WCAG 2.5.8 AA 24x24px floor. Named, already-recorded exceptions (e.g. TabPill's 32/40px sizes) get an explicit code allowlist entry with the owner sign-off it already has, never a silent pass.
findings.why: Solen already carries every piece of infrastructure this needs (Playwright, a dedicated visual CI job, a documented 44px convention) and already has one honestly-recorded below-floor exception, which is exactly the situation an automated gate exists for: catching the NEXT undersized control before it becomes a second, unrecorded exception nobody remembers approving.
findings.local_evidence: playwright.config.ts runs 3 viewports (375/768/1280) with a dedicated visual job in .github/workflows/quality.yml (confirmed present via research/GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES_2026-07-17.md section 4's own citation of both files); RATIONALE.md:485-486 records TabPill's 32/40px sizes as a deliberate, honestly-flagged below-floor exception, meaning the codebase already knows this floor gets broken sometimes but runs no automated check for the next, undocumented violation.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn -i 'target-size|axe-core' _design-system/*.md playwright.config.ts .github/workflows/*.yml -> only one RATIONALE.md prose mention of the underlying WCAG standard numbers, zero references to the axe-core package or any target-size CI rule.
findings.existing_coverage: none as an enforced gate; the 44px convention itself is well-documented (RATIONALE.md:153, the four-way WCAG/Apple/Material citation).
findings.where_it_should_live: e2e/visual/spine.spec.ts (the location research/GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES_2026-07-17.md itself already suggested) plus .github/workflows/quality.yml.
findings.enforcement: gate: @axe-core/playwright target-size rule added to the existing visual CI job.

findings.title: No law for text vertical-centering by cap-height instead of a font's full line box
findings.principle: Any button, pill, or badge that vertically centers a single line of text via flex items-center must be checked against the typeface's cap-height-to-baseline box, not its default line box, which carries ascent/descent padding that differs per font and typically reads 1-3px low at UI sizes. Measure the gap from container-top to the glyph's cap-top and from the glyph's baseline to container-bottom in devtools, tune a per-typeface line-height/padding pair once at the highest-traffic size, and reuse that tuned pair everywhere rather than trusting items-center to be correct by default.
findings.why: This is a distinct failure mode from the already-locked glyph-overshoot rule: overshoot corrects a glyph sitting off-center inside its OWN box, while this corrects the CONTAINER centering the wrong box (the font's line box, not its visible ink). Both are real, currently unchecked failure modes, but only one of them has a name anywhere in the system.
findings.local_evidence: The system's two highest-traffic commit buttons (PayConfirmStep.tsx and BookingPaymentForm.tsx, both 52px ink pills) use plain flex items-center with no per-typeface tuning value defined anywhere to check text position against.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn -i 'cap-height|leading-trim|text-box-trim|cap-top|baseline-bottom' _design-system/LOCKFILE.md _design-system/SOURCE.md _design-system/RATIONALE.md app/globals.css -> 0 hits in every file checked.
findings.existing_coverage: none, and explicitly distinct from the glyph-overshoot rule which IS covered (RATIONALE.md:144, TASTE_LOG.md:187). research/GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES_2026-07-17.md ADD item 2 named this exact gap by name on 2026-07-17 ('a grep for leading-trim/text-box-trim/cap-height/ascent/descent returns zero hits; this is not a restatement of R5') and it remains unresolved at the time of this audit.
findings.enforcement: behavioral rule today (leading-trim is still draft CSS per the cited research, so no property ships this natively yet); a design-verifier visual diff once one reference pill is tuned.

findings.title: No scrollbar-gutter law; a scroll container that toggles a scrollbar can shift adjacent content
findings.principle: Any scroll container whose content height is variable and can cross the scrolling threshold (a modal body, a bottom sheet, a sidebar list) must set scrollbar-gutter: stable, or otherwise reserve the scrollbar's width, so the browser scrollbar's appearance or disappearance never shifts the visible content sideways. Do not rely on overflow-y-auto alone on any container whose content length depends on live data the user can grow (reviews, staff lists, service lists).
findings.why: This is a well-documented, classic CSS layout-shift bug (a scrollbar appearing pushes content by roughly 15-17px in a non-overlay-scrollbar environment). It is invisible on macOS' overlay scrollbars, which is plausibly how most design review here happens, but real on Windows and Linux Chrome and inside many embedded webviews, making it exactly the kind of gap that survives visual QA done on one platform and only surfaces once real usage is broader.
findings.local_evidence: At least 5 distinct modal/sheet/dropdown wrappers in the codebase use max-h-[90vh]/85vh/80vh/60vh combined with overflow-y-auto with no scrollbar-gutter anywhere in app/globals.css; the only scrollbar rule present is scrollbar-width: none (used to fully hide the scrollbar on 2 horizontal carousel rows), which is the opposite tool solving a different problem.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i 'scrollbar-gutter|scrollbar-width|layout shift' app/globals.css _design-system/*.md -> only the 2 scrollbar-width:none hits and one unrelated font-loading layout-shift mention (RATIONALE.md:785, FOIT/FOUT); zero mentions of scrollbar-gutter or vertical-scrollbar-induced content shift anywhere in the estate.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md section 7 (new 'scroll containers' subsection) plus a utility class in app/globals.css.
findings.enforcement: checklist item today; a Playwright assertion could check zero layout-shift when a modal's content crosses its scroll threshold, but building that check is outside this read-only audit's scope.

findings.title: No systemic law for how a fixed-aspect photo frame crops a real upload whose aspect ratio doesn't match
findings.principle: Every fixed-aspect photo frame (a SalonCard photo, a PDP gallery tile, the hero grid) must state its crop anchor as part of the component's own documentation (e.g. 'center-top, never blind-center'), derived from what the photography actually shows, rather than silently defaulting to CSS object-position: center. When a real, non-seed upload arrives well outside the expected aspect range (a portrait phone photo forced into a 5:4 landscape frame), the stated crop-anchor rule must still hold rather than silently degrading to a stretched or blind-centered crop.
findings.why: Solen already solved this correctly once, for one surface, but only as a single named decision rather than a generalized rule: every OTHER fixed-aspect frame in the system defaults to plain object-cover with no anchor override, so the next uploader-facing surface will either re-litigate the same question from scratch or silently ship the center-crop the system already knows is wrong for this content.
findings.local_evidence: TASTE_LOG.md:326, 'ig4 dp-crop-bone-shaft-not-joint | APPROVED | gallery uploader gets one framing line; square photo grid crops center-top, not blind center' is the only crop-anchor decision found anywhere in the estate. SalonHero.tsx, SalonImageGallery.tsx, and SalonPortfolio.tsx's photo frames all use plain object-cover with no object-position override (CSS default = center).
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i 'object-fit|object-position|aspect-ratio|crop' _design-system/LOCKFILE.md -> 0 hits; the single ig4 TASTE_LOG line is the only crop-anchor rule in the whole estate.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the imagery FLOORS LAW (CLAUDE.md) governs whether a photo appears at all and its minimum share of the viewport, and the ig4 decision sets a crop-anchor precedent for one surface, but no LOCKFILE row generalizes that precedent to any other fixed-aspect frame.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md section 7, a new 'photo crop anchor' row alongside the container-width table, generalizing the ig4 precedent.
findings.enforcement: checklist: name the crop anchor when building any new fixed-aspect photo frame, extending the existing exists-check discipline.

findings.title: No stated ratio links a container's mobile and desktop padding; each surface picks its own step
findings.principle: State the ratio, not only the two endpoints, between a container's mobile and desktop padding (for example: desktop padding = 1.5x-2x mobile padding, rounded to the 4pt scale), so a new container's breakpoint step is derived rather than chosen fresh. Where an existing surface's ratio falls outside that stated band, name it as a recorded exception with a reason, rather than leaving it as an unexplained one-off.
findings.why: The container-width table lists absolute px-4/px-6/px-8 style values per surface but never states the rule generating the mobile-to-desktop step, so different surfaces show different ratios with no way for a reader to tell which is the intended pattern and which is undocumented drift.
findings.local_evidence: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md section 7 container table: Page outer px-4 to px-6/px-8 (1.5x or 2x), Hero content px-7 to md:px-8 (about 1.14x), Salon PDP grid px-4 to md:px-6 (1.5x), /business hero px-4 to md:px-8 (2x), FAQ section px-4 to md:px-8 (2x): three different ratios appear across 5 rows of the same table with no stated rule distinguishing intentional variation from drift.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i 'gutter ratio|padding ratio|mobile.*desktop.*padding|scal.*padding' _design-system/LOCKFILE.md _design-system/RATIONALE.md -> 0 hits; the table of values exists but the generating rule behind it does not.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the table itself is locked as frozen literals, so the VALUES are law; the delta is the missing rationale/ratio that would let a new surface derive its own step instead of picking among three existing, unexplained precedents.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/RATIONALE.md (a short new domain entry) cross-referenced from LOCKFILE section 7.
findings.enforcement: doc-only; not mechanically gate-able without a stated design intent per surface to check against.
